title: Front-end performance: Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals and WebPageTest

videos.script: The box office answers in under twenty milliseconds. Nobody waits twenty milliseconds. {{server}} They wait for a page. The page downloads a picture, runs a script, draws a list, and only then can somebody read it. {{page}} On a phone, on a train, that part is most of the wait. A load test never sees it. {{phone}} So this lesson measures the page. You will build two versions of the same one. The first is slow in four ordinary ways. A script that blocks, a picture that is too heavy, work that freezes the screen, and a banner that pushes everything down. {{four}} The second fixes all four. {{fixed}} Lighthouse loads both, pretending to be a slow phone, and gives each one a number for every complaint a visitor makes. {{report}} Those numbers have thresholds, published by Google, called the Core Web Vitals. {{vitals}} And there is a catch. A lab run is one visit, by nobody. The requirement is about real visitors, and the two are measured in different places. {{field}}
